title: The price of calm
hookLine: spilled oil, stolen wine: say, this is what peace of mind costs (Enchiridion 12)
last: CARE FOR IT LIKE AN INN.

cards: Somebody at work ate your yogurt from the office fridge. Your name was on it. In marker.
You could spend the afternoon on this: version the passive-aggressive note, investigate, tell three people. Or you could do some quick math. The yogurt cost about a dollar.
The afternoon of stewing costs a lot more. Epictetus did this math with olive oil and wine. Section twelve of the handbook puts a price tag on peace of mind, and the surprise is how cheap it is.

teach.b: If you want to make progress, Epictetus says, drop thoughts like: if I don't watch my affairs, I'll have nothing to live on.
Better, he says bluntly, to die of hunger free of grief and fear than to live in plenty and be troubled. That's strong, and he means it as a direction, not a test. Then the kitchen.
Begin with small things, he says. A little oil spilled.
A little wine stolen. Say to yourself: this is the price of tranquility, the price of being undisturbed. Nothing is had for nothing.
Tranquility here translates ataraxia: a, not, and a root meaning stirred up. Unstirred, like a pond on a still morning. Then the servant, and an honest note.
Epictetus finishes with a household scene: you call your servant and he may not come, or may come and do the wrong thing. He isn't so important, Epictetus says, that it's in his power to disturb you.
Epictetus' examples come from a world where owning people was ordinary, and he had been enslaved himself.
That's worth noticing plainly, and the point that travels still stands: other people's choices aren't a lever on your calm unless you hand it to them. So the yogurt. A dollar.
That's the price, and paid gladly, it buys an afternoon back. Small days, small prices. The expensive part is refusing to pay.

how: Some people who practice Stoicism treat small losses and annoyances as the price of tranquility, naming the cost and letting it go rather than stewing.

games.why: he says: this is the price of being undisturbed. nothing is had for nothing.

practice: Pick up something small within reach, a coin, a pen, a paper clip, and let it stand for one annoyance from today or yesterday: a spill, a late delivery, a parking ticket, the yogurt.
Hold it in your palm and name its price, out loud or inside: this is what calm costs. Then set it down, the way you'd put coins on a counter, and sit with what you bought.

wordCard.voice: Ataraxia, tranquility, the state of staying undisturbed: a little spilled oil, a little stolen wine, the small price of calm. Nothing is had for nothing. Today's word.
